question: Is terminal production-hook proof plus focused regression coverage sufficient to land this compaction fallback replay fix, or should maintainers require a live two-agent timing proof first?
rationale: The patch is narrow and source-backed, but it changes a session-state/message-delivery boundary where the original report was intermittent and timing-dependent.

options.title: Accept Scoped Proof
options.body: Land after normal exact-head merge checks because the PR exercises the production compaction hook and covers replay removal plus safe-text preservation at the fallback boundary.

options.title: Require Live Timing Proof
options.body: Ask for a real two-agent compaction recovery run showing one delivered reply and preserved safe source context before merge.

options.title: Pause For Boundary Redesign
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want replay safety handled at a broader transcript, side-effect, or API boundary instead of the fallback-source filter.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Proof
recommendation.body: Land after normal exact-head merge checks because the PR exercises the production compaction hook and covers replay removal plus safe-text preservation at the fallback boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest combined history across compaction planning, agent runtime, and inter-session provenance for this boundary choice.
